newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prosecutors probe freak German rail accident.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors probe freak German rail accident.

text.p: German prosecutors were investigating on Sunday the cause of a freak rail accident that killed six people and injured 13 when a pipe twisted off a freight train and sliced open a passenger train.
Three men and three women were killed when the 15 metre (50 foot) long iron pipe tore open a rail car filled with passengers, many of them youths beginning their summer holidays.
The accident happened just before 9 a.m. (0700 GMT) on Saturday near the town of Stadtallendorfs, 80 km (50 miles) north of Frankfurt.
The cause of the accident was under investigation. The Marburg prosecutors office was examining whether charges of negligent manslaughter and endangering rail traffic could be laid.
State prosecutor Martin Laubach said a commission was studying how the accident happened. The driver of the freight train said he did not notice anything out of the ordinary before the accident.
The prosecutors would not comment on media reports saying the accident was caused when a nylon cord holding the six-tonne pipes in place broke.

Among the six dead were three women: a 31-year-old from Ghana, a 50-year-old from Sweden, and an 18-year-old from Berlin. The three men killed were an 21-year-old from Berlin, a 32-year-old from Gross Linden and a 16-year-old from Allendorf.
Two children from Berlin, a five-year-old boy and an 11-year-old girl, were in serious condition in hospital.
The busy Frankfurt-Kassel rail line was still closed on Sunday.
The lower level of the train car was completely ripped open by the iron pipe and newspapers, lunch bags, thermos bottles, fruit, and blood-soaked clothing were strewn about the floor.

"We heard the people screaming and ran immediately over here," said Thorsten Mueller, who was playing soccer nearby with a group of friends. "There was blood and broken glass everywhere. It was brutal. I have never seen anything like this."
Other witnesses who hurried to the scene reported hearing a loud bang followed by cries from injured. "It was a really horrible bang," said one woman who lives nearby.
The train was filled with passengers taking advantage of special low weekend tariffs. There were about 300 people on board, authorities said.
